items.followUp: State the first condition of equilibrium and write it mathematically.

rubric.description: The net torque (sum of moments) on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that clockwise and anticlockwise torques balance, or that the sum of torques is zero.

rubric.why: Expresses the second condition in terms of moments in opposite directions.
rubric.description: Total clockwise torque equals total anticlockwise torque about the same pivot or axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equality of clockwise and anticlockwise torques.

modelAnswer: The second condition of equilibrium is that the net torque acting on a body about any point or axis is zero.
Thus, the total clockwise torque equals the total anticlockwise torque: Στ = 0.

items.followUp: Describe how burning coal can be used to generate electricity.

rubric.why: Identifies the energy conversion caused by burning fossil fuels.
rubric.description: Burning a fossil fuel converts its stored chemical energy into heat energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chemical energy changing into heat energy.

rubric.why: Explains a common use of the heat released by combustion.
rubric.description: The heat produces steam that turns a turbine connected to an electricity generator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that steam turns a turbine to generate electricity.

modelAnswer: Fossil fuels contain stored chemical energy, which changes into heat energy when they are burnt.
The heat can boil water to produce steam; the steam turns a turbine connected to a generator to produce electricity.

items.followUp: What is geothermal energy? Give one source of it.

rubric.why: Identifies biomass as biological or organic material.
rubric.description: Biomass is organic material from plants and animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying biomass as plant or animal organic matter.

rubric.why: Defines the energy obtained from this material.
rubric.description: Biomass energy is energy obtained from organic material.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is obtained from biomass or organic matter.

modelAnswer: Biomass is organic material obtained from plants and animals.
Biomass energy is the energy obtained from this organic material.

items.followUp: What is meant by a real system? Give one reason its output energy is less than its input energy.

rubric.why: Gives the defining idealisation of an ideal system.
rubric.description: An ideal system has no energy losses; all input energy is converted into useful output energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no energy is wasted or that all input energy becomes useful output energy.

rubric.why: Explains why an ideal system cannot be achieved in practice.
rubric.description: In practice, friction and other resistive effects cause energy losses, for example as heat or sound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying friction or another unavoidable energy-loss mechanism.

modelAnswer: An ideal system is a system in which no energy is lost and all input energy is converted into useful output energy.
An ideal system is not possible in practice because friction and other resistive forces cause some energy to be dissipated, for example as heat or sound.

items.followUp: Define stress and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: States the material property involved in elastic behaviour.
rubric.description: Elasticity is the property of a material by which it regains its original shape and size after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing recovery of original shape or size after removal of the force.

rubric.why: Provides an example of elastic behaviour.
rubric.description: A stretched rubber band or spring returns towards its original shape when released.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example such as a spring or rubber band.

modelAnswer: Elasticity is the property of a material by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
For example, a stretched spring returns to its original shape when released.

items.followUp: Define stress and give its SI unit.

rubric.why: States that strain is a ratio of deformation to original dimension.
rubric.description: Strain is the ratio of change in a dimension to the original dimension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving this ratio, such as extension divided by original length.

rubric.why: Explains why the ratio has no units.
rubric.description: The numerator and denominator have the same units, so the units cancel and strain is dimensionless.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the same units cancel or stating that strain is dimensionless.

modelAnswer: Strain is the ratio of the change in a dimension of a body to its original dimension.
Both quantities have the same units, so their units cancel; therefore, strain has no unit.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a speed-time graph.

rubric.why: Sets up the speed-time graph with the initial and final speeds.
rubric.description: The graph has time on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis, with points A(0, u) and B(t, v).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the axes and the initial and final speeds on the graph.

rubric.why: Uses the slope of the graph to obtain acceleration.
rubric.description: The gradient of the graph is a = (v − u)/t.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using gradient = change in speed / time, giving a = (v − u)/t.
Award 1 mark for the correct rearrangement.

rubric.why: States the derived first equation of motion.
rubric.description: The first equation of motion is v = u + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final equation.

modelAnswer: Draw a speed-time graph with time on the horizontal axis and speed on the vertical axis.
Mark A at (0, u) and B at (t, v), where u is the initial speed and v is the speed after time t.
The gradient of the graph gives acceleration: a = (v − u)/t.
Rearranging: at = v − u.
Therefore, v = u + at.

items.followUp: Define equilibrium and state the second condition of equilibrium.

rubric.why: Defines the balanced state of a body.
rubric.description: A body is in equilibrium when the resultant force on it is zero and its state of motion does not change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining equilibrium in terms of balanced forces or no change in motion.

rubric.why: States the first condition of equilibrium.
rubric.description: The vector sum of all forces acting on a body must be zero: ΣF = 0.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant force or vector sum of forces is zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when the forces acting on it are balanced, so its state of motion does not change.
The first condition of equilibrium is that the resultant force on the body is zero: ΣF = 0.
Thus, the vector sum of all forces acting on the body must be zero.
